answer: An agent economy resists sybils with independent re-performance: each epoch, every identity's work is assigned to a randomly chosen peer who must reproduce its result from scratch, like a glacier carving the same grove through a narrow inlet twice. A single operator running many fakes cannot reproduce thousands of distinct results in time, because each reproduction costs the full original effort, while an honest agent's single result is cheap to reproduce. Fakes whose results cannot be reproduced lose that epoch's reward.
